title: Geo commitment roadmap and fallback heuristics
content:
Purpose
This doc captures a pragmatic roadmap for committing customer workloads to geographic regions (what we call geo commitments) and a set of deterministic fallback heuristics operators and the control plane can rely on when strict pinning is unavailable. It is intended to bridge product-level policy (legal/team commitments) with the operator runbooks and the routing runtime behavior.

High-level goals
- Provide predictable semantics customers can depend on for SLA/SOC requirements (explicit commit events, rollback behavior).
- Minimize availability impact when region constraints cannot be satisfied (graceful degradation).
- Ensure auditability and telemetry for every routing decision to satisfy compliance and post-incident review.
- Keep implementation and operator surface area small: prefer policy over bespoke exception code.

Definitions (how we use terms)
- Geo commitment: An explicit customer-level binding that says "customer X sessions/data must run in region R". Can be applied at org, project, or route level.
- Strong pin: Traffic must only execute on resources whose physical or logical location is inside the committed jurisdiction (hard failure otherwise).
- Soft pin: Prefer region R but allow controlled fallback to approved alternate regions with documented reasons (used for high-availability, burst).
- Fallback window: The allowed time interval (seconds/minutes) where runtime may route to fallback region before failing.
- Commitment evidence: Audit record showing which host/region served a request, used in legal or compliance review.

Assumptions and constraints
- Private deployments (customer-managed VPCs) have different enforcement guarantees than Redwood-hosted Dedicated—this doc focuses on platform-side enforcement semantics (hosted/dedicated), with operator steps for private installs.
- We assume KV cache and tokenized artifacts may cross regional boundaries unless pinned explicitly (we must maintain explicit opt-in for caching outside region).
- Some third-party integrations (metrics sinks, KMS replicas) are region-limited; operator guidance must include these dependencies.

Roadmap (quartered milestones)
- Q4 2024: Stabilize audit schema and telemetry events for geo routing. Implement Commitment object in control plane (API to create/view/delete).
- Q1 2025: Implement soft-pin routing policy with a pluggable fallback list per commitment (primary, fallback-1, fallback-2) and a default fallback window (30s). Add operator CLI to force-fail commitments for drills.
- Q2 2025: Introduce enforcement modes: report-only, enforced-with-warnings, strict-enforced. Add per-commitment SLA metadata.
- Q3 2025: Automate canary rollout APIs for region pinning changes (A/B commit switches), integrate with Console rollouts UI.
- Q4 2025: Expand to cross-cloud residency proofs and enterprise audit exports (signed manifests).

Fallback heuristics (deterministic rules for runtime)
- Primary -> fallback-1 -> fallback-2 sequence. Each endpoint lookup returns routing candidates ordered by policy.
- Candidate selection uses this score: enforceability_score (binary for strong pin), health_score (0..100), latency_penalty (ms), and compliance_score (binary if region allowed by customer). The runtime picks first candidate with enforceability_score >= mode threshold and health_score > 50.
- If strict-enforced mode: do not route outside primary. Return 409 with "region_unavailable" to caller after a fast probe (250ms) if no healthy primary candidate.
- If enforced-with-warnings: attempt primary for 500ms total; if no success, use fallback-1 and emit commitment-violation telemetry event (tagged as auto-fallback).
- If report-only: prefer primary, but always route to next healthy candidate without failing. Telemetry event emitted but no caller-visible error.

Operator playbook (quick actions)
- Detection: Alerts should fire if: primary candidates consistently fail (>5% error rate over 5m) OR if failover count exceeds threshold (5/min).
- Immediate triage steps: 1) Check commitment object and recently applied rollout logs. 2) Query routing telemetry for request traces (search by commitment id). 3) If primary region down, set commitment to enforced-with-warnings to keep traffic flowing while tracking violations.
- Escalation: For strict customer contracts, file an incident and notify legal/compliance; preserve signed commitment evidence in blobstore and tag incident.
- Rollback: Use the rollout API to revert any recent change to the fallback list. If the control plane is unavailable, follow manual operator checklist (doc references at the end).

Telemetry and audit requirements
- Every routing decision must emit: commitment_id, timestamp, chosen_region, candidate_list, chosen_reason (health/policy/fallback), latency_ms, trace_id, operator_override (bool).
- Store commitment evidence for 365 days by default for enterprise plans; shorter retention for trial customers. Evidence manifest format: CSV line per request with fields above and a signed digest.
- SLOs to track: on-time pin adherence (percentage of requests honoring primary within 200ms), auto-fallback rate, mean time to fallback recovery.

Testing and verification suite
- Unit: simulate candidate health permutations and assert heuristics pick expected candidate.
- Integration: a synthetic workload that simulates primary region blackout for 1s/10s/1m and validates telemetry and rollback behaviors.
- Compliance test: a small corpus of sample customer commitments across EU/US/APAC that must never leave primary in strict mode; run nightly and fail build on regressions.

Compatibility notes (private vs dedicated vs hosted)
- Private: control plane may be customer-managed; provide a constrained enforcement shim and operator checklist. Default to report-only unless customer opts for stricter.
- Dedicated: platform can enforce strong pin by restricting scheduling to pinned pools; requires capacity reservation gating.
- Hosted: best-effort enforcement with documented fallback semantics; transaction-level guarantees will be weaker unless customer purchases reserved capacity.

Operational hints for cost/throughput tradeoffs
- Soft pin with a short fallback window reduces tail latency spikes at the cost of occasional cross-region token costs. Recommend: set soft-pin for high-throughput, non-sensitive routes; strict for any PII or contractual routes.
- Cache locality: when allowing fallback, ensure prefix/KV cache invalidation is consistent and shipped with the commitment change (explicit cache TTLs).

Decision log (short history of why we chose current heuristics)
- 2024-08-10: Prototype attempted naive fail-open; produced silent data-plane violations — unacceptable for enterprise.
- 2024-09-02: Chose three-tier fallback list to balance operational simplicity and customer needs.
- 2024-10-01: Added enforcement modes after legal and SRE review.

Open questions and items for legal signoff (action items)
- Should we allow cross-region KV caching for strict-enforced commitments if the cache is encrypted with region-authorized KMS? (Action: legal + security to advise, owner: Sofia M., due: 2024-11-05)
- SLA language: For enforced-with-warnings, what is the acceptable auto-fallback rate before SLA credit? (Action: Product + Finance, owner: Priya S., due: 2024-11-22)
- Retention window: enterprise vs standard (owner: Marisol R., ask Risk)

Appendix A — quick CLI snippets for operators
- View commitments: rwinfctl commitments list --org=ORG_ID --region=EU
- Force-check routing candidates: rwinfctl debug route-check --commitment=COMMIT_ID --timeout=1s
- Temporarily switch mode: rwinfctl commitments set-mode --id COMMIT_ID --mode enforced-with-warnings --reason "incident 2024-11-02"

Appendix B — manual recovery checklist (if control plane down)
- 1) Pull last-known commitment manifest from S3: s3://redwood-commitments/backups/<org>-latest.csv
- 2) Call oncall: private-deployments-pager (step in rota)
- 3) Apply emergency host filters on edge routers to prevent cross-region egress for strict customers (network team assist required).

Notes to reviewers
- This is a living doc. The implementation detail (timers, thresholds) are conservative suggestions; please add data-driven counters from production telemetry once Q4 stabilization is complete.
- If you are an operator: add any missing quick commands you rely on in the CLI snippets section.

Unresolved: need legal and security sign-off on KMS/caching item.
